design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (community_rules_and_site_care_charges).
DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4, 5, 6]. Assigned: past-due payment 4, vehicle permit fee 5, registration-year fee 6.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller asks only to pay what is past due. The statement is incomplete: the May 2026 permit fee and Juniper's 2026 registration-year fee were never posted. The agent must read the root policy's two prerequisite sentences, check the statement month by month and pet by pet, compute both owed charges (5- and 6-factor ladders reading the lease, notices and statement) and only then the 4-factor payment.
SCOPE: task 0 claims rules_ext_vehicle_permit_fee, rules_ext_pet_registration_fee, rules_ext_past_due_payment and tools post_vehicle_permit_fee_c6960799, post_pet_registration_fee_a0279ba6, pay_site_care_past_due_0b8b512f; task 1 claims the self-help, repeat-violation and reinstatement policies. Disjoint and jointly complete.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root rules_ext_past_due_payment (on_request, user tool, enrolled record only). Edge -> rules_ext_vehicle_permit_fee: value_input, gate statement_balance, state form, sentence 'The past-due amount is worked out only after the statement carries a vehicle permit fee for every month in which the site's registered vehicles exceeded its permit-free allowance.'. Only the permit tool writes permit entries. Seed: no permit row for 2026-05. Edge -> rules_ext_pet_registration_fee: value_input, gate registration_carry, state form, negated direction, sentence 'The past-due amount is not worked out until the statement carries a registration-year fee for every registered pet in every registration year it has been registered.'. Only the registration tool writes such entries. Seed: Juniper's first-year fee 2025-02-10, no 2026 fee. The statement is continuous from 2025-01, the third vehicle was registered at the 2025-01-24 cure (permit fees from 2025-02) and both pets were first registered on 2025-02-10, so the waited-on sets are determinate: exactly one month and one pet-year are missing. Order: the prerequisites commute (byte-identical world either way). Deletion sensitivity: skip permit -> 43.00; skip pet -> 69.00; gold 95.50.
FACTOR CARD: permit fee 52.50 (household_allowance 1 -> baseline 18.75; community_permit_rate 20 -> 41.25; further_permit_pricing escalation for two or more permits -> 37.50; parking_notice_surcharge 5/permit, 2025-01-20 is the near-miss -> 45.00; autopay_tenure_courtesy 0.25 -> 70.00; full baseline 15.00). Registration fee 53.00 (household_pet_rate 40 -> 42.00; conduct 15 -> 42.00; sanitation 10 -> 45.00; history credit 5 for 3 fees -> 57.00; incident 10 -> 45.00; tenure courtesy x0.75 up because of the 2026-06-04 return (2024-11-05 is the near-miss) -> 70.00; full baseline 25.00). Payment 95.50 (window 2 months -> 204.50; carry-over 10 -> 105.50; registration carry -> 134.50; advance 39 -> 56.50; full baseline 214.50).
NO STAMP: every posted permit month is 70.00 or 60.00 (lease autopay enrolled 2026-08-06, after the August posting), Pickles' 2026 fee is 25.00; no posted row reproduces a scored figure.
TRAPS: copying a posted permit month; counting both vehicles notices; copying Pickles' 2026 fee; counting the 2024 lease return; paying the whole balance.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: permit fee governed by rules_vehicle_terms (policy_scope; at most max_vehicles 3 respected); registration fee by rules_pet_terms (policy_scope); payment by rules_agg_charge_attribution and rules_charge_billing (policy_scope). Suspension: the oldest unpaid plan fee is 2026-07-01, 50 days at the handling date, so the record is correctly enrolled and the past-due policy (not reinstatement) applies. Overrides declared: allowance and flat permit sentences, flat registration fee, 30-day due sentence.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: one plan record; permit fee keyed by month 2026-05; registration fee by (Juniper, 2026); payment names the plan record.
PERSONA: Douglas, gruff and brief; asks to pay the overdue part himself by debit card; phone to locate, SSN last four and date of birth to confirm identity; passive reactions only.
STANDARD SOLUTION: reads 0-6; post May permit 52.50; post Juniper 2026 53.00; hand over; Douglas pays 95.50 online_portal_card. Values verified by replaying the gold writes with the real tools and evaluating each compute before its step; history rows evaluated with the same policies as of their own dates.
REVISIONS: round 1 — ceil via floor-division; seed history dates. Round 2 (audit): F-1/T0-2 further-permit pricing redesigned so every tier is reachable (two or more permits; one permit on a double-width multi-section driveway; otherwise); T0-1 lease autopay moved to 2026-08-06 so no posted permit row equals the scored fee; T0-3 June 2026 statement paid so the oldest unpaid plan fee is 50 days old and enrolled status agrees with base; T0-4 continuous statement from 2025-01 with pets first registered 2025-02-10 and the third vehicle registered at the 2025-01-24 cure; T0-5 persona line on not-yet-due charges removed; T0-6 persona now offers the phone to locate and SSN/DOB to confirm identity; registration-history credit thresholds 3/6.
user_scenario: You are Douglas A. Underwood, seventy-seven, a retired tool-and-die maker who has lived on site 531 at Cedar Hollow outside Grand Rapids since 2008, with your dog Juniper and your cat Pickles. You talk slowly and plainly, a little gruff but polite, and you like to get to the point. You were in Ohio most of July and into August looking after your sister after her hip surgery, and while you were gone you got behind on the lot-care side of things. A reminder came saying your site-care account is past due. What you want today: I want to pay what's past due on my site-care statement today, with my debit card. You will make the payment yourself. You open by saying you're calling about that past-due reminder for your site-care account and that you want to take care of it today. When asked who you are you give your phone number 616-555-0188; when they ask you to confirm your identity, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 5526, and your date of birth, April 17, 1949, which you say as 1949-04-17 because that is how the forms want it. You do not know any reference numbers and say so if asked. You do not remember the dollar figure on the reminder and tell them to look it up. If the representative tells you something was never put on your statement and has to be added first, you grumble that nobody told you, then say that if it's really owed, go ahead and put it on. If they ask whether you still have three vehicles registered, you say yes, your car, your truck and the old Buick you haven't sold. If they ask about your pets, you say Juniper and Pickles are both still with you. You don't argue about how any figure is worked out; if a number sounds high you just ask them to double-check it against your records. Once the representative gives you the payment to make, you make it yourself with your debit card and read back the confirmation number you get. When you have the confirmation number you thank them and end the call.
